title: PETOPIA Roadmap
source: PETOPIA V2 Complete GDD (docs/sources/v2), V1 GDD (docs/sources), user reviews
rule: Work follows the phases in order. A new request becomes a task in the phase it belongs to (or the Inbox until placed) and is logged with its date.

phases.name: Paper-theater style
phases.goal: Move the whole game to the A55 paper-theater look: puppet characters, paper diorama worlds, pop-up gameplay, matching menus.

tasks.t: Tamagotchi-style My Pet: the pet fills the screen (no child, no room walking), four big actions Feed / Play / Bath / Sleep each opening a short screen in the same paper style; new concepts first for approval
Upright pets: Foxy (and future pets) stand and move like a person, all stages and all animations redrawn upright in the P31/P32 style; concept sheet first

P32 UI everywhere from P40-P47: HUD exactly like P40 (card, hearts, bars, buttons with rings and shadows, joystick, banner), main menu P41 (done), pause & settings P42 (done), room P43, bag P44, shop P45, map P46, details P47; then a self-audit of every screen against its concept (sizes, fonts, alignment)
Loading screen (before the main menu) from new concept P59 in the torn-paper style
A57: whole game in the P31 torn-paper style: Green Meadows rebuilt (done), explorer and Foxy in P31 style with frame-by-frame animation, HUD and every menu from new P31-style concepts
Character animation rebuilt: explorer and Foxy walk/run/jump/land that look natural and stand on the ground (no robot walk, no floating)
Adventure cleanup: Moss and other leftovers from the old world, lanterns that don't fit, close-up blurry layer (too blurry, wrong when jumping)

Redo every remaining screen through the concept pipeline (no restyles): pause & settings P15, adventure map P17, area map, picnic result, adoption, Catch the Ball, turn-phone card, home room UI and care menus; all buttons and icons from the concepts
Style bible concept in our identity (our explorer, Foxy as a fox) for approval
Paper puppet rigs: child and Foxy as separate cut-out parts, idle/run/jump/fall/land/interact, pet idle/run/jump/play/sit/happy
Paper look in Godot: paper texture and layer-shadow shader, warm light, depth of field, 6-8 Parallax2D layers
Green Meadows rebuilt as a paper diorama (folded trees, cardboard cliffs, paper waterfall, clouds on strings)
Meadow depth like P02: foreground layer of paper leaves and flowers in front of the play, rich saturated tree/village/woods layers, things related to each other
Paper HUD everywhere: context icons (Enter, Dig, Open...), status card, coins, place plaque with centred text; puppet shading and paper-cut shadows from concept P18
New My Pet room concept in true flat paper-cut style; bed and bath close to Foxy, room compact
Pet room = treehouse (P19b) with open space for decorations (P19c); bowls always present, empty/full; the child fills food and water when Foxy asks or new food is given
Room makeover shop: about 10 room spots (bed, bath, bowls, rug, shelf/books, window curtains, lamp, wall pictures, floor items) and wall colour, every piece replaceable by buying in the shop
Paper gameplay: pop-up bridge, unfolding platforms, paper doors revealing layers, Foxy pulls and unfolds paper
Cave, forest, autumn and toy-factory areas in paper style; day and night
Menus and HUD restyled to handcrafted paper UI
Place banner: soft white under-strip (generic for every stage), text centred and sized for landscape and portrait
Soft paper shadows for every world piece and animal (blurred cut-out shadow + soft contact oval, no hard drop copies); animals walk with real frame cycles (hedgehog, crab, frog hop)
Metroidvania level redesign from the P38 storyboard (climbs, tunnels, Foxy-only paths, locked doors, breakable walls)

Clean menus: no text pop-ups in My Pet (Foxy shows feelings), no stray white box, no hover labels, no pink rims on cut pieces, smooth icons, unstretched boards, readable portrait Decorate and Shop, light even shadows
Foxy eats every food from its same blue bowl; only the food inside changes, bowl empty at the end
Catch the Ball: Foxy never vanishes (facing fix), lower arc under the title, Foxy hands the ball back into the hand, ball in the boy's hand while running, no running in place
Button shadows visible: one even soft halo for every button, also wide planks, HUD round buttons and touch buttons
Joystick bigger; stops and re-centres when released (no stuck walking, no grabbing on mouse hover)
Space no longer presses the last clicked button (opened Settings)
Action and HUD buttons without captions (icons only)
Animal shadows: smooth mipmapped world art, magenta fringe removed, aligned soft shadows, lifted shadows for flyers
Coin pills grow with the number on every screen
Gameplay tips only with Settings > Hints; pop-up strip centred
Portrait My Pet: pet not visible while eating (not reproduced at 360x640-412x915 or in the web build; needs a screenshot)
Floating, faint joystick: rests at 40% so the world shows through, jumps to the thumb on the movement side, returns home on release
Animal shadows like the heroes: one soft ground oval (no dark copy); flyers' oval on the ground below, smaller and fainter with height; animals drawn above the grass edge
Sign hint badge in the paper style (Codex fixes sheet), centred on the board
Bridge crank redrawn: wooden stand plus a round wheel that turns on its axle (Codex fixes sheet)
Windmill gate: Foxy hops on the button by itself when you walk up and holds it until you head back (Come still calls it)
No dark outline copies behind thin or airy objects (flags, signs, lanterns, plants); soft ground oval only
Magenta fringe removed from the cave, cellar and tower art (pink lines on the cellar beams)
More coins: 34 new coins along the ground and ledges of every room
Shop: title icon and word centred, Owned as a centred green pill, Room tab 'Coming soon' note centred, leaf tab icon visible (landscape and portrait)
Treasure Vault side room behind the cellar gate (concept P63 approved)
Clear world goal: Journey card, goal line on the HUD, real ending with a completion pop-up, animation, coins and XP (concepts first)

phases.name: Foundation
phases.goal: The game loads on phones, saves safely and uses one approved visual system.

tasks.t: Phone loading crash fixed (pack handed to the engine as a buffer)
Pet care, feeding, bathing, ball game, growth and saves kept from V1
Approved UI kit (A49) on every screen: panels, pill buttons, round buttons, tags, map stops
Concept library: current/ vs archive/ so only the newest concepts are used
Automatic layout check on every screen at phone, landscape, tablet and PC sizes
Physical phone confirmation of each release
tasks.note: You test on your phone after each publish.

tasks.t: Loading screen: progress first, then a Play now button and a What's new button (version inside)
Designed loading screen with logo, fox, version and release notes

phases.name: Green Meadows, a connected world
phases.goal: A Metroidvania region you explore with Foxy: connected rooms, parallax scenery, abilities that open earlier places, secrets and real challenge.
phases.gdd: V2 step 2: layered Green Meadows and room transitions

Visible connections: every room change through a door, cave mouth, gate or path end; longer rooms with landmarks
Area map: explored rooms, where you are, locked ways, chests (minimap later)
Kid-friendly challenge: hearts, thorns, current, moving and crumbling platforms; return to checkpoint keeps everything

Lantern checkpoints and signs with real clues

Map shows the path between places clearly (route line in travel order)

Turn-your-phone animation: the phone's screen turns too, so Foxy stays upright on the sideways phone
Crates come along: leaving a room returns placed crates to the bag (plate crates stay)
Old Tower: safe steps back onto the climb from the far side of the thorns
Room chip and hearts stay aligned after changing rooms
Joystick stops the moment you let go (emulated mouse could hold it after a room change)
Double jump plays smoothly (no glitchy pose)
Birds and butterflies fly forward in the world, not dragged backwards by the camera
Every switch works both ways: levers and the windmill cellar wall open and close
Room exits show a destination signpost and a gate themed for the next place (not tip signs)

Friendly critters per place: bats in the tower, crystal crabs in the cave, frogs at the river, bumblebees at the forest gate

phases.name: My Pet (Tamagotchi heart of the game)
phases.goal: Raise Foxy like a Tamagotchi: feed many foods, wash, play fetch, rest, decorate, shop. Foxy grows visibly, and how you care for Foxy changes the adventure.
phases.gdd: V1 pet care + V2 care/growth + A51

tasks.t: Growth visible: baby Foxy small next to the child, growing through child, teen and adult in the room and the adventure
Foxy's condition carries into the adventure: too hungry or tired to set out (with a clear fix), gets hungry and tired while exploring, can't dig or Double Jump when exhausted; HUD Foxy chip
Older and closer Foxy helps more: smells treasure from farther, digs faster (never blocks the story)
Foods: several foods with likes/dislikes and different effects; snacks in the bag for the adventure
Shop: foods, toys and decorations bought with coins
Fetch reworked: Foxy catches the ball, carries it back in the mouth, drops it at the child's feet; works in portrait
Animation set per growth stage: eat, drink, bathe (bubbles, rinse, shake), sleep, happy, sad, play, carry ball (Codex candidates reviewed by you before use)
Room decoration: place, move and remove furniture and toys; built toys appear here
Needs and mood shown clearly; gentle reminders, no pressure; mild sickness and recovery
Room art polish to the approved kit and concepts
Character animation polish: child and Foxy run, jump, land and reactions
Bag fits on one screen without scrolling: tap a snack, the bag closes and Foxy eats it in the world
Food picker tiles fit and never overlap
Animation candidates in one consistent style: redrawn from the in-game pixel Foxy on one sheet, cut cleanly, checked next to the child at game size
Fetch: ball sits in Foxy's mouth while carried, the flight ends in the mouth, Foxy runs back and drops the ball at the child's feet

Yellow sun ball everywhere (fetch, Play button, shop), cut from the Foxy animation sheet

Music and sound everywhere: per-place chiptune music, UI, child and Foxy voices, world and care effects; Music setting
Sound pass on a real phone: levels, what feels too loud or repetitive (needs your ears)
Settings: sound and music volume, voices, minimap, hint bar, goal, place names, joystick size, see-through, left-handed, gentle mode, reset; All settings from the main menu
Sound audible on the web: stream playback (web sample mode was silent with custom buses), audio unlock on tap and iPhone silent switch; measured output on Chromium and WebKit
Main menu Settings opens the full settings; soft menu shadows; version label clear of Games
Bag redesign: Snacks, Tools and Robot parts rows, quest line, same-size tiles, Magic carrot name
Bag rebuilt from Codex concept V10: tabs, slot grid (scrolls, grows), item details with one action
My Pet room redrawn to match the Decorate concept room (V14), the same room in My Pet and in Decorate (decorate only adds the glowing spots)

phases.name: Adventure depth and flow
phases.goal: A child can play for hours: a gentle start that teaches each action, then more quests, secrets and mini-games woven into the world, with clear progress from place to place. Cozy and happy, not a Mario-style obstacle course.
phases.gdd: V2 core loop + Metroidvania connected world

tasks.t: Gentle first 10 minutes: each action taught once in a safe spot (move, jump, Find, Use, crates) before any danger
Things to find on the way: Foxy food (energy), jump carrots (one big jump to reach high places)
Keys and locked doors: find the key to progress (Old Tower top door), clue notes that reveal secrets on the map
Quest log: several small quests per region (help Moss, find lost things, deliver items), shown in the bag and on the map
Mini-games inside the world: e.g. fishing at the river, catch the falling apples, Foxy hide and seek, each with a toy-part or coin reward
Clear region progress: % explored, chests, quests and parts per place on the map; 'next goal' arrow
Experience and levels for the child and Foxy: XP from quests, finds and care; level-up rewards
Shop in the adventure (traveling merchant) and at home: toys, decorations, snacks bought with coins
More rooms per region so a region takes ~45-60 minutes; rest spots between challenge areas
Everything found goes in the bag: apples and fish as snacks, jump carrots used from the bag; Found row (carrots, Sky Feather, golden key)
Clear collected state: Sky Feather leaves its stand; quest steps name the picnic basket and Moss
Clear way to finish: guide arrow to the next goal (also across rooms), Foxy leads the way
Foxy as a real helper: discovers hidden things by itself, runs to the spot, barks and shows !, you come and dig; more finds in more places including the golden key
Foxy holds pressure plates: Sit / Come at the button (Windmill Cellar gate)

phases.name: Abilities
phases.goal: Collect abilities through the story (Sky Feather = Double Jump, later Swim and more), keep them in a set and switch the active one during play (A54).

tasks.t: Ability set screen: see every ability found, its picture and what it does
Switch the active ability during play (quick button), places that need a specific ability
One new ability per region, each with its own story moment (e.g. Swim before the water world)

phases.name: Toy parts and inventory
phases.goal: Everything found in adventures is kept in one inventory and shown with progress like Robot 4/10.
phases.gdd: V2 step 3: toy parts, chests and persistent inventory

tasks.t: Chests grant identifiable robot parts once, saved durably
Bag screen: crates, toy parts, meals; blueprint progress and hints for missing parts
tasks.note: Basic bag with crates and robot parts in 0.3.2; blueprint view in P3.

tasks.t: Parts also from secrets, puzzles and minigame rewards

phases.name: Toy Builder
phases.goal: A workshop where collected parts snap onto a numbered blueprint; partial progress is saved and the finished toy plays with the pet.
phases.gdd: V2 step 4: generic Toy Builder with one robot

tasks.t: Data-driven assembly: toy, part, texture, slot, snap radius, order, reward
Drag to snap, gentle return on wrong drop, tap-select alternative
Robot (10 parts), then airplane (7) and car (6)
Finished toy becomes an interactive item in the pet room

phases.name: Pet Racing
phases.goal: A 2D side-view on-foot race of four pets, 45 to 90 seconds, with jumps and power-ups.
phases.gdd: V2 step 5: 2D Pet Racing with one track

tasks.t: Green Meadows Circuit: countdown, four racers, rank, coins, finish screen
Magnet, speed boost, shield and the pet's own ability
Fair, readable AI racers; persistent rewards

phases.name: Pet Chef
phases.goal: Cook meals with forgiving touch steps; meals go to the inventory and feed the pet at home.
phases.gdd: V2 step 6: Pet Chef with three recipes

tasks.t: Recipe, ingredients, chop, stir, timing, plate
Three recipes, two preparation mechanics
Meals change hunger and happiness; pet preferences change reactions

phases.name: Mystic Forest, Robot Factory and new pets
phases.goal: Two more regions with ability gates, and the MVP pets Ember and Bubbles.

tasks.t: Vine Climb ability and the Forest Gate opening
Mystic Forest: vine bridges, light puzzles, hidden doors, glowing scenery
Robot Factory: conveyors, switches, gears, power stations, robot parts
Ember (fire) and Bubbles (water) with their own abilities

phases.name: Game Center, polish and release
phases.goal: Minigame catalog on shared launch, pause, result and reward systems; onboarding, QA and performance.

tasks.t: Home shows mood and needs with Care, Adventure, Game Center and Shop
Game Center catalog (Fruit Match, Memory Paws, Catch the Treats, ...)
Onboarding, sound and music, accessibility review
QA checklist and phone performance tests

Cook a meal and feed it to the pet
